terms.gloss: enter, record (in a register or notebook)
terms.grammar: verb, irregular, transitive; with in + accusative
evidence: Cic. Sull. 42: in tabulās pūblicās relātum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: With in tabulās, in commentārium, in librum: to enter something in a record. Its commoner senses are “bring back”, “report” and “refer” (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.52: litterīs (Lewis & Short, s.v. mandō)
terms.comment: To write something down so that it is kept: of history, a speech, what someone said.

terms.gloss: write out in full; put on record
evidence: Traupman 177: est perscrīpta (a motion put on record)

phrases.latin: cum scīrem ita indicium in tabulās pūblicās relātum
phrases.english: since I knew that the evidence had been entered in the public records in that form

sources: Lewis & Short: refero · Lewis & Short: mando · Lewis & Short: perscribo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 177, checked against the searchable text of the book.
Citations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them and have not been checked against an edition.
